purpose: Present one source-grounded package for the seven decisions that can change security, platform support, public identity, or compatibility.

decisions.topic: Fork and untrusted pull-request runner policy
decisions.recommendation: Use hosted runners for fork and untrusted pull-request code; permit an ephemeral equivalent only when it has no persistent workspace, shared package store, secrets, or reusable process state and has an equivalent teardown proof.
alternatives: Ephemeral isolated runners with explicit lifecycle, secret, cache, and artifact controls.
decisions.impact: Hosted-only is slower or more expensive for some lanes; an ephemeral exception preserves throughput but expands infrastructure and proof obligations.
decisions.reversibility: High for workflow routing; changing runner class later does not alter package APIs, but a relaxed policy requires revalidating all fork isolation tests.
decisions.compatibility: No runtime API change; changes CI scheduling, cache behavior, and release evidence requirements.

decisions.topic: Proxy credential transport for model-authored execution
decisions.recommendation: Keep proxy URLs and credentials out of model-authored PTC and workflow subprocess environments, argv, diagnostics, and logs; route any needed egress through a host-owned capability or separately authorized broker with redaction.
alternatives: Direct model-authored egress with an explicitly sanitized, credential-free proxy endpoint.
Model-authored code runs direct and cannot use the host proxy.
decisions.impact: Some model-authored scripts lose ambient proxy access; a broker preserves selected network capability but adds an authorization and protocol surface.
decisions.reversibility: Medium: tightening is straightforward, while reintroducing proxy access requires new threat-model, logging, and subprocess tests.
decisions.compatibility: The current PTC launch already starts with an empty child environment; the decision fixes the public security invariant and any supported exception mechanism.

decisions.topic: Dynamic extension deployment, consent, CSP, and defaults
decisions.recommendation: Support only an explicit deployment matrix; require host-verifiable consent for untrusted or browser execution; use restrictive CSP and Trusted Types-compatible delivery; allowlist or verify publishers; and disable dynamic runners and installed bundles by default.
alternatives: Host-only dynamic execution with browser halves disabled.
Browser execution with an explicitly accepted unsafe-eval/inline policy and per-install consent.
Allow arbitrary sources under an administrator-controlled registry and signature policy.
decisions.impact: The recommended policy reduces convenience and may require package signing or deployment configuration; broader policies retain functionality while increasing trust and CSP exposure.
decisions.reversibility: Medium: defaults can be relaxed later, but browser CSP and consent changes require new compatibility and security evidence.
decisions.compatibility: Changes plugin installation defaults, browser execution availability, caller permissions, and supported headless/SDK/ACP deployments.

decisions.topic: Aggregate HTTP and RPC buffered-memory admission
decisions.recommendation: Use one instance-owned limiter shared by buffered HTTP and RPC bridge entry points, reserve conservatively before intake, fail fast at a bounded budget with a deterministic rejection, and release only after cancellation, response disconnect, and owned handler work are quiescent.
alternatives: Bounded FIFO admission instead of immediate rejection.
Retain only the existing per-request cap.
decisions.impact: Concurrent large requests may be rejected earlier or queued; conservative reservations trade throughput for predictable memory use.
decisions.reversibility: High at the configuration level if the limiter is explicit; changing semantics later requires replaying concurrency and cancellation tests.
decisions.compatibility: Changes HTTP status/RPC error and retry behavior, deployment configuration, and the accepted concurrency envelope for buffered routes.

decisions.recommendation: Make the public close/disposal promise complete only after the relevant WebSocket reaches CLOSED or emits its close event, with explicit timeout, error, already-closed, repeated-close, and late-callback behavior.
alternatives: Keep logical disposal as the postcondition and document that physical closure may follow.
Split close initiation from a separately awaited physical-closure API.
decisions.impact: Callers may await longer and must handle timeout/error; logical disposal can preserve responsiveness but does not prove transport quiescence.
decisions.reversibility: Medium: adding a separate wait API is additive, while changing the meaning of close can affect every disposer and teardown test.
decisions.compatibility: Changes the awaited lifecycle contract for gateway client disposal and late WebSocket callback handling.

decisions.topic: Client-domain ownership and shared document API placement
decisions.recommendation: Move composer bodies into the input domain, Browser view bodies into the browser domain, keep top-level assembly as the only cross-domain composition owner, and expose only the minimal document contract/registry/tab-lifetime API through approved shared modules; keep renderer internals private.
alternatives: Widen contract/ to expose the existing runtime modules.
Create a narrower shared adapter package and keep the registry implementation private.
Move all presentation files into their feature domains while preserving only assembly re-exports.
decisions.impact: The source layout and package-private imports change across 38 edges; focused GUI and real-composition tests must prove registration and lifecycle equivalence.
decisions.reversibility: Medium to low after public re-exports or generated graphs change; source moves are reversible before downstream consumers adopt new paths.
decisions.compatibility: May change package-private source paths and generated module-graph output; approved public exports and runtime behavior must remain compatible.

decisions.topic: Fork publication identity and public source exports
decisions.recommendation: Use a fork-owned namespace and repository identity for any independently publishable package; keep unapproved fork-only packages private or unpublished; remove `./src/*` from ordinary runtime exports unless the maintainer explicitly authorizes publishing source trees with a compatibility, license, and packed-install policy.
alternatives: Retain the upstream namespace and metadata only with explicit upstream publication authority.
Publish a bounded fork-owned package subset while keeping the rest private.
Publish source trees and support `./src/*` as a versioned compatibility surface.
decisions.impact: A namespace migration requires package and consumer mapping; removing source exports may require migration notes for source-import consumers; retaining them expands the published surface and review burden.
decisions.reversibility: Low after registry publication or consumer adoption; package identity and source-export changes require versioned migration and deprecation rather than silent rollback.
decisions.compatibility: Directly changes package names, repository metadata, dependency resolution, packed-install contents, NodeNext consumers, and the supported public API.

commands.summary: Fork pull-request workflows exclude fork code from persistent runners.
Four security/process files pass 56 tests with one environment skip under serial file execution.

limitations: The user-approved recommendations authorize implementation and compatibility validation only. They do not approve AAA-008's unresolved request-count oracle, external publication, registry writes, push, merge, release, or the final AAA verdict.
